item.title: URGENTE - El Senado paraguayo rechaza por amplia mayoría el pedido de prórroga de Santiago Peña
item.description: La Cámara de Senadores de Paraguay rechazó, con 39 votos en contra y dos abstenciones, la solicitud de 72 horas presentada por el presidente Santiago Peña para preparar su defensa en el juicio político. Las abstenciones correspondieron a Celeste Amarilla y Silvio “Beto” Ovelar. Tras la decisión, el proceso continuará en 30 minutos y el mandatario o su equipo jurídico deberán comparecer ante la Cámara Alta. Publicado también por: France 24 - Español. Fuente: France 24 Español.

item.title: ‘A global political awakening’: how gen Z protests are sweeping the world
item.description: From Serbia to Bangladesh and India to France, young people are pushing back against authoritarianism and reshaping political landscapes In Brazil, they rallied online by the millions, sharing videos and spreading memes. In Serbia, they cycled across Europe and ran ultramarathons to make their voices heard. Both movements burst into international public view last month as they became central during election campaigns to the pushback against authoritarianism. What they also offered, however, was a window into a wider phenomenon playing out across the globe, as youth-led movements reshape… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.description: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. item.description: Tras la debacle en las midterms, Donald Trump y los republicanos coinciden en atribuir el descalabro electoral a la guerra en Irán y al impacto económico para los estadounidenses. Al interior del partido, no obstante, varios apuntan el dedo directamente contra el presidente, mientras él busca desligarse de la derrota. Trump defiende que "valió la pena" abrir el conflicto, pero figuras potencialmente presidenciables, como J. D. Vance, Marco Rubio o Ron DeSantis, intentan tomar distancia. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24
